lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Date of birth and nationality are personal details not conventionally included on this résumé.
items.because: They are not meant to be weighed as qualifications and may distract from relevant experience and skills.

items.says: The experience entries are not in newest-first order.
items.because: Brightcart is more recent than Pinecrest, so the current order makes the work history harder to scan chronologically.

items.says: Experience should appear before education.
items.because: Leading with the degree rather than the analyst work does not foreground the candidate's relevant professional background.

items.says: The daily-checking stopping rule does not establish significance for a conventional unadjusted A/B test.
items.because: Repeatedly checking and stopping when p < 0.05 raises the false-positive rate above 5%.

items.says: The A/B-test bullet gives the stopping procedure but no outcome or resulting decision.
items.because: Without what the test found or whether checkout performance changed, the value of the work is hard to assess.

items.says: The p-value checking procedure is described at unnecessary length.
The A/B-test bullet feels separate from the analyst story in this entry.
items.because: A reader may not see how the claim supports the candidate's analyst profile.

items.says: The call-center analysis bullet should come before the A/B-test bullet.
items.because: Its operational impact is the stronger opening for the entry.

items.says: “Analyzed 18 months of call-center data” does not identify the analysis that found the evening peak.
items.because: One specific method would make the candidate's contribution easier to assess.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person pronoun in a résumé bullet.
“Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in July 2022.
The fraud-automation bullet buries its result under unrelated duties.
items.because: The list delays the clearest evidence of impact and makes the automation harder to recognize on a quick scan.

items.says: “Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract” does not show what was automated or how.
items.because: The reader cannot see the technical or process skill involved.

items.says: The claimed 10-hour monthly saving has no stated measurement or comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot tell how the saving was calculated or what it was compared with.

items.says: The dashboard description does not explain how lapsed buyers were identified or defined.
items.because: A reader cannot see the analytical skill behind the dashboard.

items.says: The retention lift is buried after the dashboard description.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the increase in repeat purchase.

items.says: The revenue-report method follows the result and can be shortened.
The described join does not find customers with no orders.
items.because: Starting from orders cannot retain customers with no matching order, and a null customer name can indicate an unmatched customer record.

items.says: The bullet does not say what the no-orders finding was used for or what changed as a result.
items.because: Without a downstream action or outcome, the value of the work is unclear.

items.says: The null-name implementation detail is lengthy and obscures the finding.
The gerund phrase is the subject of “raised,” rather than the candidate, and the long methods list delays the result.
items.because: The activities become the subject of the main verb, while a scanning reader may miss the increase in campaign-attributed orders.

items.says: The funded recommendations appear only after the presentation description.
items.because: The funding outcome is the clearest evidence of impact, but readers meet it after the setup.

items.says: The dashboard-self-service phrase is wordy.
The 12% mean absolute error is not interpretable as a percentage without its scale or denominator.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the percentage is relative to.

items.says: The bullet does not identify the forecasting approach.
items.because: A brief method detail would show what forecasting skill produced the result.

items.says: The change from 300 to 200 hours is a 33⅓% reduction, not a 50% reduction.
items.because: The decrease is 100 hours out of the original 300.

items.says: The replay result has no stated comparison baseline.
items.because: The reader does not know which rebalancing plan or scenario the counts represent.

items.says: The empty-station-hours result should lead the project bullets.
items.because: It is the project's strongest line and would make the operational result more immediate.

items.says: The figures show a 15-percentage-point increase in hit rate, not a 15% increase.
items.because: The change from 60% to 75% is 15 percentage points, or a 25% relative increase.

items.says: The bullet does not define what counted as a forecast hit.
items.because: Without the criterion for a correct prediction, a reader cannot interpret the hit rates.

items.says: The pantry-line result is delayed until after the method and “so.”
items.because: A scanning reader reaches the impact only after the analysis description.

items.says: The bullet does not give the number of unique households identified.
items.because: Without the count, a reader cannot tell the scale or value of the new baseline.

items.says: “After the project ended” is unnecessary timing detail.
